newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO FACE TRICKY START IN BORDEAUX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO FACE TRICKY START IN BORDEAUX.

text.p: Monaco, bidding to become the first side for five years to retain the French championship, face a tricky start to a new league campaign against Bordeaux on Friday.
Since Marseille won the last of their five consecutive titles in 1993, Paris St Germain, Nantes and Auxerre have all failed to defend their titles.

Monaco look hard-pressed to buck the trend. They lost several key players in Sonny Anderson, Emmanuel Petit, Patrick Blondeau, Enzo Scifo, Marco Grassi and Gilles Grimandi, although the arrival of Japhet N'Doram, Christophe Pignol and Christophe Pignol has limited the damage.
Lilian Martin, Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou, John Collins and Sylvain Legwinski are all injury doubts for Friday when the new-look side will have an early test of their credentials.
"Frankly, we wish we could have started against an easier opponent," said general manager Henri Biancheri.
"Bordeaux are, with Paris and Marseille, in the leading bunch. They signed up good players and if everything clicks straightaway for them, we'll be in danger."
Monaco coach Jean Tigana will have no secrets from Bordeaux's new manager Guy Stephan, who was his closest aide two seasons ago in Lyon.
Stephan has his problems of his own, however, as Bordeaux lost no less than 15 players in the close-season after former coach Rolland Courbis left for Marseille.
"With each new league season, you start from scratch, with changed teams of unknown potential. What's good is that we seem to have adapted quickly," said Monaco new recruit Pignol.

Playmaker Ali Benarbia is also optimistic. "We had a good physical preparation and we're all working very seriously," he said. "There's nothing like starting against strong opposition to get right into it."
Stephan pins high hopes on the pairing of strikers Jean-Pierre Papin and Lilian Laslandes, who linked well in the 5-1 thrashing of Guingamp in a friendly.
But he recognises that Friday will be a different matter. "Monaco are no Guingamp," he said.
